label: UniFi Cloud Gateway Fiber
description: Ubiquiti UCG-Fiber - 10G cloud gateway: 1x 10GbE RJ45, 2x 10G SFP+, 4x 2.5GbE RJ45 LAN (1 PoE+, 30W); 5 Gbps IDS/IPS.

poe.note: 30 W, and one PSE port. The rendered tech-spec table prints the budget without naming a port - "PoE Budget = 30W" and "Voltage Range PoE Mode = 50-57V" beside "2.5 GbE RJ45 = 4 (2.5G/1G/100M/10M) / 10 GbE RJ45 = 1 (10G/2.5G/1G) / 10G SFP+ = 2 (10G/1G)", and its 'Max. PoE Wattage per Port by PSE' group is present but empty (https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/ucg-fiber, read 2026-11-19); the 'Port 1 PoE+' reading in research/ubiquiti-cloud-gateway-poe-budgets.md therefore recorded the budget and left the row without a PSE. The vendor's own store page for the same SKU (displaySku "UCG-Fiber (30W)") states the class and the count in its key features: "Integrated 4-port switch with (1) PoE+ port" (https://store.ui.com/us/en/products/ucg-fiber, read 2026-11-19). So one of the four 2.5G RJ45 ports is 802.3at. Which one is not published on either host, so Port 1 carries it - the same convention as devices/zyxel/gs1900-24ep.json, where the datasheet gives the count and the guide withholds the numbering. 30 W budget = one 802.3at port at its 30 W PSE ceiling, so the budget never binds above a single full-power AP.

notes:
Power: none of these copper ports accepts PoE. Vendor page https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/ucg-fiber (HTTP 200, 667,242 B, read 2026-11-19, server-rendered tech-spec table) says "Power Method = DC jack (54V DC/1.1A)"; a box fed from mains, a USB-C supply or a DC jack has no PoE-PD front end, so WAN / Port 2 / Port 3 / Port 4 now declare poeIn: false. Without that declaration the engine's isPoePd() match on "unifi" gave each silent copper port a 12.95 W 802.3af draw - the defect PR #2118 and PR #2121 fixed across the UXG family (refs #130).

**LAN bank (layer 2), read 2026-11-21.** Both vendor surfaces carry `MAC Address Table Size = 4,000` and `VLAN/Subnet-based Traffic Segmentation = True`, beside `2.5 GbE RJ45 = 4` - https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/ucg-fiber (HTTP 200, 667,242 B), and the storefront payload repeats both rows (HTTP 200, 595,995 B; https://store.ui.com/us/en/products/ucg-fiber answers 307 to its own category path, so the redirect was followed). `LACP Port Aggregation` is the one L2 row this box leaves Empty on both surfaces, so the four 2.5G sockets bridge without a LAG and the row declares `l2-forward` without claiming bundle support. A 4,000-entry MAC table is a bridge forwarding database, so Port 1-Port 4 forward at layer 2 (MAC learning + flooding). Measured on the pre-change spec: hosts on Port 1 and Port 2 in 192.168.1.0/24 could not resolve each other's ARP, and `switchport access vlan 10` answered "cannot switch frames: it has no l2-forward capability". `no switchport` still makes a LAN port routed; the WAN port keeps its address.
